A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Topology of Reasoning study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite appendix renumbering and additions.

before.justification: V1 reports original hidden-state graph analyses across mathematical benchmarks, model sizes, and layers, plus graph measurements from the authors' SFT experiments.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds non-mathematical benchmark results, automatic cluster-labeling results, and an s1-versus-LIMO graph analysis.

M1.justification: The proposed newline segmentation, hidden-state averaging, K-means clustering, directed graph construction, graph metrics, and SFT procedure remain unchanged. The new GPT-4o-mini labeling experiment interprets existing clusters without modifying graph extraction or model inference.

E1.justification: V3 extends evaluation beyond mathematics to StrategyQA multi-hop question answering and BIG-Bench LogicalDeduction (Appendix E). It also uses LIMO as input data in comparison with s1-v1.0 (Appendix L), while retaining the original mathematical benchmarks and s1 training datasets.

E2.justification: The evaluated reasoning-model/base-model comparisons remain unchanged; the new non-math experiments reuse DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B and Qwen2.5-32B. LIMO supplies comparison data to the same Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct model, rather than introducing an evaluated LIMO-trained model or competing reasoning algorithm.

E3.justification: Original graph metrics, layer settings, and SFT hyperparameters are retained. Added protocols include GPT-4o-mini thematic labeling of the 200 clusters and comparing s1/LIMO prompts using Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct explicitly without fine-tuning. These are new analyses, not revisions to the original training experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a substantive examination of cluster semantics through automatic labels and reasoning-step examples. Appendix L adds a separate analysis of dataset-associated graph structure without fine-tuning. Figure 3 also replaces several illustrative cases; the existing clustering-sensitivity, layer, model-size, and checkpoint analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V3 continues the existing sample-distribution reporting practice. Its new checklist asserts statistical significance but supplies no additional uncertainty estimates or statistical procedure.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial results while retaining the original quantitative findings. At layer ratio 0.1, Figure 10 reports distilled/base cycle ratios of 0.89/0.07 on StrategyQA and 1.00/0.33 on LogicalDeduction. Table 1 adds semantic cluster findings, and Figure 16 reports larger diameters and higher cycle counts for s1 than LIMO under the new no-fine-tuning comparison.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of segment representations, graph construction, cycles, diameter, clustering coefficients, and small-world index are retained. Segment/token index changes are notational; neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction broadens its contribution statement from analysis across mathematical reasoning datasets to analysis across multiple datasets, consistent with the new non-math coverage. The central abstract and discussion claims about cyclicity, diameter, small-world structure, and SFT-data effectiveness remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 interprets the new cluster labels as planning and reassessment behaviors, the non-math results as evidence of generality, and the s1/LIMO differences as indicators of data quality. Appendix M newly acknowledges the absence of feature-level and circuit-level analyses and the unresolved emergence of graph properties during training.

D1.justification: V3 adds an implementation-repository link, explicit model-checkpoint URLs missing from v1's footnotes, and the GPT-4o-mini labeling prompt. The hardware and detailed SFT configuration remain unchanged. These are documented access and reproducibility improvements; availability of the linked resources is not verified by the PDFs.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations for the labeling model, non-math datasets, and mechanistic-interpretability and training-dynamics research discussed in the expanded limitations. The main related-work argument and reasoning-graph novelty positioning remain intact. LIMO was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are largely preserved. V3 makes localized wording and notation edits, converts numbered related-work subsections into run-in headings, updates the publication footer, inserts appendix sections and cross-references, and appends a NeurIPS checklist.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is substantially redrawn with revised sample selection, axes, and trajectory coloring, while Figure 1 corrects its mismatched question. V3 adds a full-page semantic-example table, the six-panel non-math Figure 10, and the s1/LIMO Figure 16. Retained appendix displays are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's mathematical evaluations and few illustrative node labels, v3 provides useful evidence of non-math generality and richer cluster interpretability, alongside clearer visualizations and access information. The gains remain limited: the s1/LIMO experiment does not test fine-tuning benefits, and the new checklist's significance assertion lacks additional uncertainty analysis. The revision strengthens support and transparency without resolving the acknowledged gap between graph correlations and actionable training guidance.
